name: Blood Knight
body:
Blood knights are warriors who treat combat as art. They do not fight for carnage, but for sport. Through pain and the measured rhythm of battle, they seek perfect understanding of the self. Each drop of blood spilled is an offering. Whether in solemn duels or against legions, the Blood Knight stands serene in the storm, blade steady, spirit unmoved.

Role: A Blood Knight is a frontline combatant who thrives in sustained battle. They are rewarded both by sustained aggression as well as powerful hexes they can put upon foes.

Alignment: Chaotic Neutral

Hit Die: d10

Class Skills

The Blood Knight’s class skills are Appraise (Int), Bluff (Cha), Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Disguise (Cha), Handle Animal (Cha), Heal (Wis), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (local) (Int), Knowledge (religion) (Int), Perception (Wis), Profession (Wis), Ride (Dex), Sense Motive (Wis), Spellcraft (Int), Swim (Str), and Use Magic Device (Cha).

Skill Ranks per Level: 4 + Int modifier.

Class Features

All of the following are class features of the blood knight.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency

Blood knights are proficient with all simple and martial weapons. They are also proficient with light, medium, and heavy armor but not shields.

Duelist’s Challenge (Ex)

At 1st level the blood knight learns to channel his aggression against a single foe, focusing on bringing them down. This is a swift action, and against the subject of this challenge they receive a +1 to attack and damage rolls, however they suffer a -2 penalty to AC against the attacks of anyone who isn’t the subject of their duelist’s challenge. This lasts until the opponent is slain or the blood knight willingly gives up the duel (or they accept the opponent conceding the duel), and an opponent cannot be the target of this ability again for 24 hours after its effects end. A blood knight can only have one target for their challenge active at one time (unless they can split the bonus among targets, see below).

Every 4 levels thereafter, the bonus increases by 1. In addition, the blood knight can choose multiple targets for their challenge so long as their bonus is +2 or higher. When doing so, they choose who they receive their bonus(es) against. If an opponent is slain or is no longer affected by the duelist’s challenge, the bonus that was allocated to that opponent is reallocated to any remaining opponents in the battle (if any) at the blood knight’s discretion. For example, a level 13 blood knight chooses to split their +4 into a +2 for opponent A, and a +1 for opponent B and C. If opponent C were to die, they can choose to reallocate the +1 against opponent A (for a total of +3) or against opponent B (for a total of +2).

Blood knights can use duelist’s challenge once per day, however its uses can be recovered by spending 1 combat fervor.

Combat Fervor (Ex)

At 1st level the blood knight is satiated when blood is spilt, and this death fuels them in the upcoming battles. They receive a pool of combat fervor which starts at 0 points and can increase to a maximum amount equal to their blood knight level (minimum of 1). The following actions can result in them gaining combat fervor points. Spending points from combat fervor is a free action, though these points might be spent in conjunction with an ability which takes a standard or swift action for example.

Critical Hit: Each time the blood knight confirms a critical hit, they gain 1 combat fervor. Confirming a critical hit on a helpless or unaware creature or a creature that has fewer Hit Dice than half the blood knight’s character level doesn’t earn them combat fervor.

Killing Blow: When the blood knight reduces a creature to 0 or fewer hit points while in combat, they gain 1 combat fervor. Destroying an unattended object, reducing a helpless or unaware creature to 0 or fewer hit points, or reducing a creature that has fewer Hit Dice than half the blood knight’s character level to 0 or fewer hit points doesn’t earn them combat fervor.

Tempered Aggression (Ex)

At 2nd level the blood knight is a force to be reckoned with and will stop at nothing to pursue their prey. Against a target of their duelist’s challenge, the blood knight adds their Charisma modifier (if any) as a bonus to AC and all saving throws against them. This does not stack with abilities such as a paladin’s divine grace which grants similar bonuses.

Adrenaline Rush

At 3rd level and every 3 levels thereafter the blood knight learns new ways to utilize their combat fervor, and make the battlefield truly their domain. The DC of any adrenaline rush is equal to 10 + 1/2 blood knight level + the blood knight’s Charisma modifier. Unless specifically noted, an adrenaline rush cannot be selected more than once.

A complete listing of adrenaline rushes can be found here: Adrenaline Rush

Spells

Beginning at 4th level, a blood knight gains the ability to cast a small number of divine spells which are drawn from the paladin and antipaladin spell lists. A blood knight must choose and prepare their spells in advance.

To prepare or cast a spell, a blood knight must have a Charisma score equal to at least 10 + the spell level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against a blood knight’s spell is 10 + the spell level + the blood knight’s Charisma modifier.

Like other spellcasters, a blood knight can cast only a certain number of spells of each spell level per day. Their base daily spell allotment is given on Table: Blood Knight. In addition, they receive bonus spells per day if they have a high Charisma score (see Table: Ability Modifiers and Bonus Spells). When Table: Blood Knight indicates that the blood knight gets 0 spells per day of a given spell level, they gain only the bonus spells they would be entitled to based on their Charisma score for that spell level.

A blood knight must spend 1 hour each day in quiet prayer and meditation to regain their daily allotment of spells. A blood knight may prepare and cast any spell on the paladin or antipaladin spell lists, provided that they can cast spells of that level, but they must choose which spells to prepare during her daily meditation.

Through 3rd level, a blood knight has no caster level. At 4th level and higher, their caster level is equal to their blood knight level – 3.

Chaotic Crusader: Blood knights are able to prepare spells from the paladin or antipaladin spell list except any spells which have the [good] or [evil] descriptor, and spells like protection from evil which can be targeted against law instead always are that variant (for example, they can prepare protection from law but not protection from law/good).

Blood knights are able to sacrifice spells known in favor of learning a Hex from the shaman or witch classes. They must meet all other prerequisites for the hex, and the saving throw uses the blood knight’s Charisma modifier instead.

Blood Hex

At 4th level and every 4 levels thereafter the blood knight gains a blood hex as a bonus feat, and similar to if they were a shaman or witch they can use blood hexes an unlimited number of times per day, but still cannot target the same creature with the same blood hex more than once every 24 hours. They use their Charisma modifier for the saving throw DCs of these blood hexes.

When selecting blood hexes, they ignore all ability score and skill rank requirements. Otherwise, they must meet all other prerequisites when selecting a blood hex.

Still Standing (Ex)

At 7th level the blood knight receives Diehard as a bonus feat without needing to meet the prerequisites (if they didn’t already have it), and they add their blood knight level to the amount of negative hit points they must reach before dying. They do not suffer damage from taking a standard action if that action is being used to attack, however they suffer damage normally for any other standard action.

Flow of Battle (Ex)

At 10th level the blood knight learns to understand instinctively how to fight their opponents given time fighting them. They receive a +1 insight bonus to damage at the end of every round they choose to attack a target of their duelist’s challenge. This bonus stacks to a maximum bonus equal to their blood knight level, and this bonus only applies to anyone who is subject to their duelist’s challenge currently. This bonus ends if they attack a target who isn’t a subject of their duelist’s challenge, or if they do not attack on their turn at all.

Crimson Meditation (Ex)

At 11th level the blood knight can choose to spend a full-round action to close their eyes and steady themselves, monitoring their breathing as well as calming their heart rate. This temporarily sates their bloodlust and puts them into a tranquil state of calm, but also helps them realign themselves to their true goals. After using this, they can choose a single effect which lasts multiple rounds which is affecting them (such as a spell or status effect), and end it immediately. If this is a disease, poison, or curse they are treated as casting the spells remove disease, neutralize poison, or remove curse respectively. Effects which are permanent cannot be ended this way (except for curses), and only one effect can be ended at a time in this manner. If the blood knight fails to remove the effect, they cannot try again for the next 24 hours (however they can still try to remove other effects).

Sanguine Perfection (Ex)

At 14th level the blood knight automatically confirms critical hits so long as the opponent they are attacking is currently suffering from the bleed status effect.

Scarlet Crucible (Ex)

At 19th level the blood knight becomes immune to bleed damage, gains DR 5/-, and they under a constant freedom of movement effect, rendering them unable to be affected by difficult terrain or stopped from pursuing their prey.

Avatar of Battle (Su)

At 20th level the blood knight has become a paragon of war, of battle, and of might. They double the bonus from duelist’s challenge (making it a +10), and they maximize the damage of any bleed damage they deal to opponents. Opponents suffering from bleed damage within 30 feet of the blood knight must cast greater restoration or other similar high level healing spells to end bleed, preventing common healing spells from ending its effects.

Code of Conduct

A blood knight must be of the chaotic neutral alignment to take levels in the class, and loses all blood knight class features if they cease being chaotic.

This code is a set of philosophical guidelines that inform their actions, not a list of absolute laws that bind them. It represents a personal commitment to a way of life centered on challenge and self-reliance.

Combat is Truth: Blood knights believe that a warrior’s true character—their courage, skill, and will to live—is revealed only in the life-or-death struggle of battle. Debate and diplomacy are fleeting, but the outcome of a mortal struggle is an undeniable truth. They cannot deny a warrior’s willingness to engage in a duel, and stopping a duel is seen as a great dishonor without good reason.
Seek the Worthy Challenge: Stagnation is a form of death. A blood knight must actively seek out powerful opponents and difficult fights to test their limits and grow stronger. They cannot shy away from a tough fight just because it’d be hard. If it’d be suicidal, they aren’t obligated to fight. But just because it sounds hard, a fight isn’t to be denied.
Mercy is a Choice: A defeated foe has proven themselves unworthy. Sparing them is the victor’s prerogative, a display of confidence or a dismissal of a lesser threat. Cruelty for its own sake, however, is a waste of energy that could be spent seeking the next challenge.
Freedom Above All: Blood knights answer to no master, no king, and no law but their own strength of arms. They will not suffer a leash, and they will fight anyone who seeks to impose one upon them. This doesn’t prevent them from working in groups, or higher-ranking individuals, but it means they will refuse their commands if they disagree—sometimes obviously, sometimes less so. Some even show no signs of disagreement outwardly, but will then choose to ignore those commands when the time comes. This, however, is no excuse for flippancy.

A blood knight who willingly and permanently adopts a Lawful alignment or who persistently and deliberately avoids conflict finds their inner fire extinguished. They lose their connection to their combat fervor and all associated class abilities until they atone by seeking out and overcoming a truly worthy challenge on their own.
